title: Classical Variation (6.Be2)
intro: Meet 6.Be2 with 6...e5. Answer 7.O-O with ...Nc6, reroute ...Ne7, ...Nd7 and ...f5 against d5, and chase 7.Be3 with ...Ng4.
variation: d2d4 g8f6 c2c4 g7g6 b1c3 f8g7 e2e4 d7d6 g1f3 e8g8 f1e2

steps.text: In the Classical Variation, White prepares to castle with 6.Be2. Now that your king is safe, it is time to strike in the centre.

steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e5 to fight for central space and open your c8 bishop.
steps.ifRight: Now White must choose between castling, closing with d5, or trading on e5.

steps.text: Put pressure on d4 so White commits in the centre.
steps.hint: Develop your queen's knight to c6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...Nc6 to attack d4 and invite 8.d5.
steps.ifRight: White usually closes the centre with 8.d5.

steps.text: Step back to e7 to clear the c-file and prepare ...f5.
steps.hint: Move the c6 knight to e7.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8...Ne7 so your knight helps on the kingside and frees the f-pawn after ...Nd7.

steps.text: In the Petrosian System (7.d5), White closes the centre before castling. Secure the c5 square for your knight.
steps.hint: Push your a-pawn two squares to stop b4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...a5 (or 7...Nbd7): 7...a5 stops White's b4 expansion and secures c5 for your b8 knight.

lessons.title: Meeting 7.dxe5 and 7.Be3
lessons.summary: Recapture ...dxe5 and know the ...Nxe4 tactic; chase 7.Be3 with ...Ng4.

steps.text: Instead of 7.O-O, White sometimes tries the Exchange Variation with 7.dxe5.
Recapture with the pawn to keep lines open and control d4.
steps.hint: Take back on e5 with the d-pawn.
steps.ifRight: Remember that e5 is protected: if White trades queens and takes e5, ...Nxe4 wins it back.

steps.text: After 8.Qxd8 Rxd8, if White gets greedy with 9.Nxe5:
Win back the pawn and threaten a discovered attack on the e5 knight.
steps.hint: Capture on e4 with your knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9...Nxe4: White's e5 knight is attacked by your g7 bishop and c3 is hanging.
steps.ifRight: Black regains the pawn with active piece play on the d-file.

steps.text: Another popular choice for White is 7.Be3, guarding d4 without closing the centre.
Harass the e3 bishop immediately with your knight.
steps.hint: Jump to g4 with your f6 knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...Ng4 (or 7...Nc6) to chase the bishop away and clear the f-pawn.
steps.ifRight: After 8.Bg5 f6 9.Bh4, Black attacks smoothly with ...Nc6 and ...g5 or ...Nh6.

lessons.title: The Kingside Attack
lessons.summary: Bring the knight back to f6, push ...f4, and open lines with ...g5.

steps.text: White plays 11.Bd2 to prepare Rc1 and c5 on the queenside. Meanwhile, Black builds a decisive kingside storm.
Bring your d7 knight back to f6 so it eyes e4 and clears the c8 bishop.
steps.hint: Put the d7 knight on f6.
steps.ifWrong: Play 11...Nf6 to pressure e4 and prepare ...g5.
steps.ifRight: With ...Nf6, White must guard e4 with f3.

steps.text: Gain kingside space and lock in White's dark-squared bishop.
steps.hint: Push the f-pawn forward to f4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 12...f4 so you can march ...g5, ...h5 and ...g4.
steps.ifRight: Now Black's kingside attack rolls forward with ...g5 and ...Rf7-g7.

steps.text: White strikes on the queenside with 13.c5.
Keep pushing your kingside attack to open files against White's king.
steps.hint: Push the g-pawn two squares to prepare ...g4.
steps.ifWrong: Play 13...g5 to open the g-file with ...g4.
steps.ifRight: Black's pieces pour towards g2 and h2 while White's queenside play is slower.
